info.name: Deep One Dwarf
info.description: The Deep One Dwarf (Y'ha-nthlei) species from Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024).
info.author: MonkeyDM

element.name: Deep One Dwarf
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: Far removed from the splendorous halls of their ancestral kingdoms, the dwarves of Luyarnha have undergone a profound transformation, the likes of which none of their kin foresaw. These once grand merchants perpetrated a sin – coveting that which was not rightfully theirs – and for this dereliction of morality, they begot a curse of unspeakable malevolence, condemning their blood to the compelled service of He Who Lies Dreaming.

His Blessing. Their very nature was irrevocably altered, much like those who dwell beneath the fathomless depths of the ocean; relinquished was their mortality, traded for the cold embrace of eternal slavery. They would never perish, but instead live out their days alongside He who had walked the earth long before the advent of humankind and would endure their demise for wretched ages, forever bound as pawns in the insidious machinations of their infinite master. Their tragic fate – wrought by their own rapacious avarice – is the exorbitant price they paid for their crime, and one they cannot escape.

Deceptive Appearance. This curse has warped their flesh, normally so averse to magic, and created within them gates of eldritch arcane, imparting them with the peculiar ability to cloak their twisted forms, using illusions that can deceive even the keenest adventurers into seeing them as bona fide dwarves.

Accursed Immortality. Despite possessing full control of their mental faculty from a young age, their physical form twists and contorts as the impossible weight of the gift of the Slumbering One scrapes them minute after minute. Their once sturdy limbs warp and bend in grotesque fashion, their eyes become sunken and hollow, and their skin takes on a sickly gray pallor. The sanity of their younger days begins to slip away, leaving them at the mercy of His malevolent dreams and to dwell within their once dwarven flesh. This destiny – a fate more dreadful than death – is something that their aging mind anticipates with glee.

ul.li: Age. Deep One Dwarves mature much faster than humans, reaching maturity at the age of 10. They cannot die of old age; instead their aging mind progressively loses grip over their body, turning them into brainless servants of He Who Lies Dreaming when they reach 50 years of age.

description.p: As a Deep One Dwarf (Y'ha-nthlei), you have these special traits.
Amphibious. You can breathe air and water.

Cosmic Knowledge. Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of an eldritch item or construction, you are considered to have proficiency and Expertise in the History skill.

Dreamer’s Curse. Your mind is clouded by the dreams of the Slumbering One, and you find it hard to discern between reality and dream. You have Disadvantage on ability checks and saving throws to discern illusions.
Guiding Light. You know the Dancing Lights cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.

Illusory Body. Although your body is covered in tentacles, clams, seashells, and other eldritch appendages, you are covered by an illusion that makes you appear like a typical hill dwarf to others. Other Deep Ones can see through this illusion. You have Advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks against creatures that can't see through this illusion.
Otherworldly Resistance. You have Resistance to Cold damage. You also have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
Slumbering Legacy. You are descended from the Slumbering One and receive a supernatural boon from your ancestry. Choose one of the following benefits:

ul.li: Coiling Arm. Your arm is nothing but a writhing mass of tentacles that flail in the air. On your turn, immediately after hitting an enemy with a melee attack, you can make an Unarmed Strike using the Grapple option against it as a Bonus Action (normal grappling restrictions apply).

Brutal Pincers. Your forearm becomes a massive pincer, which you can use to make Unarmed Strikes. If you hit with it, you deal Piercing damage equal to 1d6 plus your Strength modifier, instead of the Bludgeoning damage normal for an Unarmed Strike. If you hit a creature you are grappling, the damage die becomes a d10 instead. You can’t use this arm to make any precise hand manipulations.
Mucoid Extremities. Your hands and feet are palmed and covered in cups. Your Swim Speed increases to 35 feet, and you gain a Climb Speed of 20 feet.

description.p: OPTIONAL: Dreamer’s Gift. Your devotion to the cosmic being that warped your species is rewarded. When you reach character level 5, you gain the following benefits:

ul.li: Whenever you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can draw upon your master’s powers to succeed instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until the Dreamer has replaced one of your D20 Tests with a 1. The GM decides when this unfortunate moment happens.
You are immune to the Curse of the Slumbering Moon.
